feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-2 controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.15, ki 0.4, base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction) with one geometry change: the sensor span is widened from x = ±0.04 m to x = ±0.07 m, with the same five sensors, y = 0.05 m, the 16 mm footprint and the same weights. Evidence: the best raced design (iteration 1, score 38.61) and iteration 2 (38.47) both ended all 60 trials off_track with 0 finishes. Each trial logged exactly one line_loss_event, and max_error sat at 0.0607 to 0.0615 on every track. Changing kp, sensor_size and ki barely moved any of these numbers, so the gains are not the main driver. The narrow span is a plausible cause, because the tape can leave the array when lateral error is only about 0.02 to 0.03 m. The change is a clean single-variable test, the design is valid, and it is not obviously broken. The outer sensors at ±0.07 m sit outside the 0.12 m body, which the contract allows (limit ±0.08 m). The inner sensors still set the signal scale, so straight-line behaviour should be unchanged. Approving it now gives the first telemetry on whether geometry, rather than gain, is the limit. Judge the result by line_loss_events, max_error and progress per track, not by score alone.

What to change after the race, depending on what it shows:
- If line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 with progress well above 0.14, keep the wider span. Then raise base_speed toward 1.6 to recover completion_time, and only then revisit kp and kd.
- If line_loss_events stays at 1 per trial with the wider span, the span is not the sole cause. Test line_loss = search_left or search_right in place of last_direction, since the direction of the loss has never been tested.
- If the wider span lowers line loss but steering_oscillation rises well above the 0.06 to 0.14 range seen so far, reduce kp toward 1.5 before changing the span again.
requested_changes: If the wider span removes line loss (line_loss_events near 0, max_error under 0.06), keep geometry.sensor_positions at x = -0.07, -0.035, 0, 0.035, 0.07 with y = 0.05, and raise controller.base_speed to 1.6 to recover progress and completion_time.

If line_loss_events stays at 1 per trial with the wider span, set controller.line_loss = search_left or search_right in place of last_direction, which has never been tested (iterations 0 to 2 all used last_direction and all failed the same way).

If steering_oscillation rises well above the 0.06 to 0.14 range seen in iterations 0 to 2 with the wider span, lower controller.kp to 1.5 while keeping kd 0.15 and the wider sensor span, because the span may make the signal more sensitive.
